name: memory-graph
description: Arches-inspired RDF knowledge-graph memory: MCP server + context-file protocol + distill skill

pane.title: Memory graph pane
pane.description: auto: the pane opens itself on the first graph tool call. manual: only /graph-panel opens it. off: no pane, and graph tool calls show in the transcript as normal. Memory recall and capture run either way.

review.title: Periodic graph review
review.description: Every few days, end a turn by asking for a graph health fix-up (over-long names, orphans, missing links).

answer_questions.title: Answer questions from memory
answer_questions.description: When a prompt contains a question the memory graph fully understands (even one buried in a long prompt), run it and add the answer to the context as memory. Half-understood questions only get the usual pointers.

answer_max_questions.title: Questions answered per prompt
answer_max_questions.description: How many questions in one prompt are tried.

answer_max_rows.title: Rows per answer
answer_max_rows.description: Rows added per answer; the rest are counted, with a pointer to memory_ask.

answer_coverage.title: Answer strictness
answer_coverage.description: Share of the question that must match the graph before it is answered (0.5 to 1). Lower answers more questions, and risks answering the wrong one.

server.title: Memory server
server.description: Where the memory graph runs. The default, http://127.0.0.1:8848, is this machine's own server: one graph for every chat, started automatically at session start and kept running (or run it as a service: deploy/systemd/). Set your hosted memory server (e.g. https://memory.example.com) to share one memory across every machine and the Claude apps; see docs/REMOTE.md.

server_token.title: Memory server token
server_token.description: The hosted server's token (its MEMORY_GRAPH_TOKEN). Leave empty for this machine's own server. Stored in secure storage.

lookups.title: Memory lookups with a server
lookups.description: Only applies to a hosted server. server: recall and question answers run on the server, which sends back just the text to add, so this device never downloads the graph (best for phones and small devices). local copy: download the graph (refreshed at most once a minute) and look it up on this device, which keeps working briefly offline.
